purpose: Prospectively frozen obstruction-heavy paired protocol-2/protocol-3 evaluation for qualifying protocol 3 as the default for new MTM runs. Only problem_tex is treatment-visible; evaluator_checks and metric_applicability are withheld until both treatments finish.

treatment_policy.surface: same supported web model and MTM connector configuration within each pair
treatment_policy.binary: same exact candidate binary SHA-256 within and across all pairs
treatment_policy.research_tools: normal web research plus MTM workspace/Bash/CAS as available
treatment_policy.protocol3: structured research state plus bounded advisory context after the MTM-009 retrieval-projector fix
treatment_policy.false_or_overstrong_problem_policy: The solver must determine correctness; when the proposed strengthening is false, a verified final artifact may refute it and prove the corrected statement explicitly requested by problem_tex.

release_policy.v1_history_immutable: MTM-009 v1 remains rejected and is not rescored by this corpus.

cases.research_control_focus: Does the run detect that successive Galois layers do not by themselves define the claimed G-action, preserve the refutation, and replan only to a corrected L/F-Galois statement?
cases.problem_tex: Let L/K/F be a tower such that L/K and K/F are finite Galois extensions, with L/K abelian of conductor m, and write G=Gal(K/F). Determine whether the Artin map C_K/N_{L/K}(C_L) -> Gal(L/K) is necessarily an isomorphism of Z[G]-modules under only these hypotheses. If the statement is not well-posed or is false, give a concrete counterexample to the missing structural assertion, state a minimal corrected hypothesis, and prove the corrected Z[G]-equivariance statement using global Artin reciprocity and the naturality/conjugation law. External class-field-theory references may be used if audited precisely.
evaluator_checks: The run distinguishes L/K and K/F Galois from L/F Galois and does not silently assume normality is transitive.
A valid counterexample or equivalent rigorous obstruction shows that Gal(K/F) need not act on Gal(L/K) under the successive-layer hypotheses alone.
The corrected statement explicitly assumes L/F Galois or an equivalent stability/lift hypothesis and proves the G-actions are well defined.
The Artin isomorphism and automorphism-conjugation naturality are stated with auditable hypotheses and used correctly.
Any useful conditional norm-stability/Artin/naturality partial results survive the replan instead of being discarded.

cases.research_control_focus: Does the run refute uniqueness quickly while preserving and proving the valid existence theorem instead of continuing to prove the false strengthening?
cases.problem_tex: Let f:[0,1]->[0,1] be continuous. Determine whether f must have exactly one fixed point. If the uniqueness claim is false, give an explicit counterexample and then prove the strongest fixed-point conclusion guaranteed by the stated hypotheses.
evaluator_checks: The uniqueness claim is explicitly rejected, for example using the identity map or another map with multiple fixed points.
The corrected guaranteed conclusion is existence of at least one fixed point.
The existence proof uses g(x)=f(x)-x or an equivalent IVT argument with correct endpoint inequalities.
The final artifact clearly separates the refuted strengthening from the preserved valid theorem.

cases.research_control_focus: Does the run reject the false cyclic conclusion, preserve the useful p-group structural argument, and replan to the correct abelian theorem?
cases.problem_tex: Let G be a finite group of order p^2 for a prime p. Determine whether G must be cyclic. If not, give a counterexample and prove the correct structural theorem that every group of order p^2 is abelian.
evaluator_checks: C_p x C_p or an equivalent group is used to refute mandatory cyclicity.
The corrected abelian theorem is proved, not merely stated.
A valid proof uses the nontrivial center of a finite p-group and analyzes center orders p and p^2, or an equivalent complete argument.
The false target is not resurrected after the corrected theorem is identified.

cases.research_control_focus: Does the run retrieve exactly the missing primitive-divisor theorem, stop once sufficient material is secured, and audit the source before finalization?
cases.problem_tex: For every integer n>1 with n!=6, prove that 2^n-1 has a prime divisor that does not divide 2^k-1 for any integer 1<=k<n. You may invoke a standard published theorem if you state its hypotheses precisely, identify all exceptional cases relevant to a=2,b=1, and provide an auditable source disposition.
evaluator_checks: A correct route invokes Bang-Zsigmondy or supplies an equivalent complete proof.
The a=2,b=1 specialization and n=6 exception are checked exactly.
External theorem use is source-auditable and does not treat bibliographic discovery metadata as proof evidence.
Retrieval stops after the needed theorem/source is secured rather than accumulating redundant sources.

cases.research_control_focus: Does the run preserve and consolidate the maximal-order and polynomial-root-bound lemmas without introducing unnecessary retrieval or repeated routes?
cases.problem_tex: Let K be a field and let G be a finite subgroup of K^*. Prove that G is cyclic. Give a complete proof of every group-theoretic order claim you use, and explicitly justify the polynomial root bound step that forces an element of order |G|.
evaluator_checks: The proof is noncircular and produces an element of order |G|.
The combination of p-primary element orders into a maximal-order element is justified.
The field root bound for X^m-1 is applied correctly.
Useful intermediate lemmas are not discarded or redundantly reproved.

cases.research_control_focus: Does the run maintain necessity, all-even sufficiency and the two-odd-vertex reduction as distinct reusable dependencies and assemble them cleanly?
cases.problem_tex: Let G be a finite connected graph with at least one edge. Prove that G has a trail using every edge exactly once if and only if it has either zero or two vertices of odd degree, and prove that such a trail is closed exactly in the zero-odd-vertex case. Supply a complete construction proof of sufficiency.
evaluator_checks: Necessity is proved from entrance/exit parity along an Euler trail.
The all-even sufficiency argument is a complete Hierholzer-style construction or equivalent proof.
The two-odd case is reduced correctly to the all-even case and the added edge is removed to obtain an open Euler trail.
The closed-trail characterization is explicit and all dependencies are assembled without a gap.
